contributions.headingText: Cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma (CMTC) is a malignant thyroid tumour with a particular growth pattern secondary to constitutive activation of the WNT/β-catenin pathway that can occur with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) or sporadically.
2D10.Y & XH1YZ3 Other specified malignant neoplasms of thyroid gland & Cribriform carcinoma, NOS
Not recommended: cribriform morular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma; papillary thyroid carcinoma, cribriform morular variant.
CMTC is usually multifocal and/or bilateral in FAP, whereas sporadic cases occur as a solitary nodule {10229505; 20878367; 21455198; 29239041}.

Almost all CMTCs (97%) occur in young women, with 89% of cases occurring in individuals aged < 40 years (mean: 28 years, range: 8–69 years) {29320754}, including paediatric patients. The M:F ratio is 1:31–61 {29320754; 29785019}. As many as 53% of CMTC cases are associated with FAP {29320754}. Tumours may present as a painless mass, hoarseness, or dysphagia, or they may be incidentally discovered on ultrasound.

In review of 129 CMTCs in the English-language literature, 63% of reported cases were from Asia, 26% from America, and 11% from Europe {29320754}. The frequency of thyroid carcinoma in FAP has increased with screening ultrasound and FNAB {29785019}.

In patients with FAP, CMTC is secondary to germline APC pathogenic variants. Somatic mutation resulting in permanent activation of the WNT/β-catenin signalling pathway is responsible for sporadic tumours {29785019}. Female sex is a risk factor {21878742; 29785019}.

Most germline APC pathogenic sequence variants in FAP with thyroid tumours occur in exon 15 (codons 463–1387), and codon 1061 is a hotspot for hepatoblastoma and CMTC {10634400}. APC mutation leads to a truncated APC protein, which is unable to contribute to β-catenin proteasomal degradation. Stabilized β-catenin is translocated into the nucleus and binds LEF/TCF proteins, leading to constitutive expression of WNT target genes involved in proliferation and loss of differentiation {29785019}. In FAP with multiple CMTCs, each tumour has a different somatic APC variant (second hit) {11106555}. Second-hit somatic variants in KMT2C and KMT2D have been described in some familial CMTCs {32024448}.

Somatic alterations involving RET (in the form of rearrangements) {9916927; 11232035}, PIK3CA {26054797}, and KRAS {24702198}, as well as TERT promoter variants {27688081}, may be additional effectors of the WNT/β-catenin pathway in familial and sporadic CMTC {29785019}.

CMTCs in FAP are often multifocal (4–13 foci), bilateral, and small; sporadic tumours are larger (mean: 30 mm), single nodules {34019236; 7698732; 10229505; 21455198; 29785019; 31469036}. CMTCs are well circumscribed or encapsulated, solid (but may be cystic), and white-tan {29785019}.

CMTCs are circumscribed or encapsulated and may appear lobulated due to fibrous septa {20878367; 29785019; 7698732}. Angioinvasion occurs in 30% of cases and capsular invasion in 40% {29785019}. CMTCs have an admixture of growth patterns not seen in other thyroid carcinomas {20878367; 7698732}. As originally described, CMTCs display “an intricate blending of cribriform, follicular, papillary, trabecular, and solid patterns of growth, with squamoid morulae” {10229505}. The cribriform structures are composed of anastomosing bars and arches, without intervening fibrous stroma, that merge with tubular follicles that lack colloid {10229505; 29785019}. Papillae and pseudopapillae are lined by tall, cuboidal or pseudostratified cells, and trabecular areas show spindle cells reminiscent of hyalinizing trabecular tumour {10229505; 21455198; 29785019}. Squamoid morulae are whorls of spindle to ovoid cells that lack keratinization and show nuclear clearing due to biotin accumulation {10229505; 29239041; 29785019}. Psammoma bodies are rare {29320754; 29785019}. With these distinctive features, the tumour was initially called the cribriform-morular subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma {10229505}. But correlation between the tumour’s morphological features and recently understood molecular alterations brought about a name change to CMTC {20966648; 21455198; 29785019; 31217615; 34019236}.

Immunohistochemistry

Aberrant strong nuclear and cytoplasmic β-catenin staining is the hallmark of this thyroid tumour {21455198; 29239041; 29785019}. CMTC is positive for thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF1, clones SPT24 and 8G3G7/1), various keratins, EMA, ER, and PR, and negative for CK20, calcitonin, and WT1 {18081818; 23161723; 24702198; 26054797; 29239041; 29785019}. Thyroglobulin expression is typically negative; however, focal nonspecific diffusion-type staining can occur due to entrapped non-tumorous thyroid follicles {34019236}. PAX8 immunohistochemistry using either the monoclonal BC12 antibody or polyclonal antisera shows no or only focal weak staining in these tumours {34019236}. Morulae are negative for keratin 34βE12, thyroglobulin, TTF1, PAX8, ER, PR, and E-cadherin, but they stain for CDX2, CD10, CD5, and CK5 {18081818; 23161723; 24702198; 26054797; 29785019; 34019236}. The Ki-67 proliferation index is usually < 5%. High-grade CMTCs have increased mitotic activity, necrosis, and a Ki-67 index of 15–60%; they may have neuroendocrine differentiation, and they can occur in both sporadic and familial settings {19095577; 23349472; 30176755; 30376202}. In a study of 33 CMTCs, high-grade features were present in 2 sporadic CMTCs and in none of the FAP-associated CMTCs {34019236}.
Findings in paediatric patients have been reported but are not unique {19534622; 20091902}.

Evaluation for germline APC pathogenic sequence variants is desirable in patients with CMTC. About 85% of germline APC variants are in exon 15, usually outside the mutation cluster region {10634400; 29785019}. In familial and sporadic cases, constitutive WNT/β-catenin pathway activation is evidenced by strong nuclear β-catenin immunostaining – a hallmark of CMTC and an important diagnostic criterion. BRAF variants are absent.

Essential:

  • A well-circumscribed or locally invasive TTF1-positive thyroid neoplasm
  • Diffuse nuclear β-catenin expression
  • Predominant complex architecture including cribriform areas and squamoid morulae, with no colloid formation

Desirable:

  • Cribriform areas: positive for pancytokeratin, ER, and PR; negative (or focal weak) reactivity for PAX8; negative for thyroglobulin
  • Morulae: positive for CD10, CDX2, CD5, and CK5; negative for TTF1, PAX8, thyroglobulin, ER, and PR
These tumours are staged according to the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) eighth-edition TNM system.

At presentation, CMTC is associated with lymph node metastases in 12% of cases and distant metastases in 3%, with an overall cancer mortality rate of 2% {29320754}. High-grade CMTCs behave aggressively {23349472; 27688081; 30376202}.
